problem_title: Why pull requests stall in engineering teams
problem_subtitle: Responsibility on PRs is almost always implicit. Reviewers do not know they are blocking work. Authors do not know when a reviewer is waiting on a reply. The result is days of silent drift.
without_item_1_body: Reviewers receive 20+ GitHub notifications daily and miss the initial request.
without_item_2_body: The author fixes comments, but GitHub does not make it clear that the ball is back in the reviewer court.
without_item_3_body: Engineers are forced to play detective in Slack: “Hey, can someone review #182?”
without_item_4_body: While waiting, base branches move, tests rot, and rebases become painful.
with_item_1_title: Single source of truth in the PR:
with_item_1_body: A pinned card shows state, blocker, and time in state right at the top of the conversation.
with_item_2_body: When author pushes commits after review, Baton instantly flips the state to “Re-review Due”.
with_item_3_body: Exactly one targeted nudge sent only when the threshold expires. Never spam.
with_item_4_body: Reviewers see PRs waiting on them in one clean queue. No manual searching needed.
how_title: From GitHub webhook to unblocked PR
how_subtitle: Baton is purely event-driven. On every pull request action and on a safety sweep schedule, the state is re-evaluated using standard GitHub APIs.
how_step_1_body: GitHub webhook fires with HMAC-SHA256 signature verification. Baton reads review states, checks conclusion, and mergeability status. It never requests or reads source diffs.
how_step_2_body: A pure state machine determines which of the 8 canonical states applies, who owns the next move, and calculates the exact duration the PR has been waiting in this state.
how_step_3_body: Baton updates its pinned comment, synchronizes the baton:* label, and if the time exceeds your configured grace period, sends exactly one polite @-mention to the blocker.
states_subtitle: Explore the exact rules Baton uses to assign ownership, labels, and thresholds. Every state has a clear definition based entirely on verifiable GitHub data.
features_title: Built for engineering teams that ship daily
features_subtitle: No fluff, no noisy notifications, no heavy dashboards nobody opens.
feature_status_card_body: Baton maintains one single, always-updated status comment at the top of the pull request. State, current owner, duration in state, and next unblocking action are always visible.
feature_labels_body: One canonical baton:* label mirrors the PR state in real time. Works seamlessly with your existing GitHub search filters, notification routing, and triage workflows.
feature_nudges_body: At most one nudge per state, sent only after your configured grace period (e.g. 24h, 48h). Mentions only the person who can unblock the PR, never spamming the whole team.
feature_engine_body: Reviews, review requests, CI checks, merge conflicts, and draft status feed into a verifiable finite-state machine. No heuristics, no AI hallucinations in the critical path.
feature_move_body: A clean developer dashboard grouping PRs by who needs to act next. Your queue is front and center so you can unblock teammates first thing in the morning.
feature_intelligence_body: Facts collected from the GitHub API, with every claim linked to the file or response it came from. Asking a question the collected evidence cannot answer returns “no evidence” rather than a confident guess.
feature_permissions_body: Baton requests only Pull requests and Issues read/write (for comments/labels), plus read-only Checks and Metadata. It never requests Contents, ASTs, or Secrets.

security_title: Baton never stores your source code
security_body: Baton requests only the GitHub permissions it uses. Repository intelligence reads the file tree, the package manifest, and CODEOWNERS so it can describe how a repository is built; those reads are used to derive facts and are discarded, and no file contents are retained. Baton does not request Workflows or Secrets. Write access is strictly limited to posting PR comments and managing state labels.

oauth_error_exchange_failed: GitHub rejected the sign-in credentials. Confirm the OAuth Client ID and Client secret, and that the callback URL is registered on the GitHub App.
oauth_error_github_api: GitHub could not complete the sign-in on its end (GitHub API error). Please try signing in again in a moment.
oauth_error_state_mismatch: Your sign-in request expired or was replayed. Please sign in again from the header. No harm done, just retry.
oauth_error_iss_mismatch: Sign-in was rejected for security reasons (unexpected OAuth issuer). Please try signing in again.
oauth_error_server_error: Sign-in could not be completed because the service database is currently unavailable. Please try again shortly.
oauth_error_db_misconfigured: Sign-in could not be completed because the service database is not configured on this deployment.
oauth_error_db_unreachable: Sign-in could not be completed because the service database could not be reached. Please try again shortly.
oauth_banner_unconfigured: GitHub sign-in is temporarily unavailable on this deployment because OAuth credentials are not configured. The GitHub App install flow still works.
oauth_banner_failed: GitHub sign-in failed. Please try again, or install the GitHub App directly from the header.
oauth_banner_denied: GitHub sign-in was cancelled. No problem, you can keep browsing or install Baton from the header.
select_prompt: Select a state to view deterministic logic & nudge rules:
matrix_awaiting_review_trigger: PR opened, non-draft, reviewers requested or required by CODEOWNERS, 0 review decisions submitted yet.
matrix_awaiting_review_nudge: Dispatches at most 1 targeted @-mention to requested reviewers. Timer resets if author pushes commits.
matrix_awaiting_review_action: Review the PR changes and submit Approve or Request Changes.
matrix_awaiting_review_after_fix_trigger: A reviewer previously requested changes or commented, and author subsequently pushed new commits.
matrix_awaiting_review_after_fix_nudge: Mentions only the reviewers whose feedback was addressed. Spares reviewers who already approved.
matrix_awaiting_review_after_fix_action: Verify the new commits resolve the prior objections.
matrix_changes_required_trigger: At least one reviewer submitted ‘Request Changes’.
matrix_changes_required_nudge: Reviewers are silenced. Author is nudged only after the grace period expires without new commits.
matrix_changes_required_action: Push changes or reply in thread to resolve reviewer concerns.
matrix_ci_failing_trigger: One or more required check suites or status contexts concluded as failure or timed out.
matrix_ci_failing_nudge: Strict safety rule: Reviewers are never nudged while CI is broken. Author is gently notified.
matrix_ci_failing_action: Inspect CI logs, resolve tests/lint, and push fixes.
matrix_conflicts_trigger: GitHub reports mergeable = CONFLICTING against the base branch.
matrix_conflicts_nudge: Alerts author that the branch has drifted out of sync with main.
matrix_conflicts_action: Rebase onto base branch or merge target and resolve conflicts.
matrix_ready_to_merge_trigger: Approved by required reviewers, all CI checks passed, zero merge conflicts.
matrix_ready_to_merge_nudge: Nudges author or maintainers if PR sits unmerged despite all lights being green.
matrix_ready_to_merge_action: Perform merge (squash, rebase, or merge commit).
matrix_blocked_on_checks_trigger: CI check suites are in-progress; mergeability cannot be evaluated yet.
matrix_blocked_on_checks_nudge: Silent state. No one is nudged while automated jobs are still compiling or testing.
matrix_blocked_on_checks_action: Wait for CI pipelines to complete.
matrix_draft_trigger: PR is explicitly marked as draft by the author.
matrix_draft_nudge: Completely passive. Reviewers are never pinged on work-in-progress drafts.
matrix_draft_action: Mark as ready for review when prepared.
sim_1_trigger: PR opened 2 days ago; review requested from @sarah-chen; no review submitted yet.
sim_1_nudge: Friendly nudge: PR #247 has been awaiting review for 48h. @sarah-chen could you take a look when you have a moment?
sim_1_rule: Deterministic Rule: Open + Non-Draft + Pending Reviewer Request + Checks Green → State = AWAITING_REVIEW. The first-response threshold elapsed, so exactly 1 nudge dispatched.
sim_2_next: Address feedback on auth middleware in src/auth/session.ts
sim_2_trigger: @sarah-chen submitted a review with ‘Request changes’: ‘Please ensure token expiry handles UTC timezone skew’.
sim_2_nudge: Timer active. The author is reminded once the grace period expires without new commits.
sim_2_rule: Deterministic Rule: Latest review decision is CHANGES_REQUESTED. The baton immediately passes back to the author. Reviewers will NOT be nudged.
sim_3_next: Verify fix commit 4d92fa1 for UTC timezone skew
sim_3_trigger: @dev-alex pushed new commit 4d92fa1 (‘fix: enforce UTC epoch in session verification’).
sim_3_nudge: Within the grace period, so no reminder is sent yet.
sim_3_rule: Deterministic Rule: Previous review was CHANGES_REQUESTED, but the author pushed new commits. State flips to RE_REVIEW. Timer resets to 0.
sim_4_nudge: Reviewers spared. Baton prevents premature review requests while CI is red.
sim_4_rule: Deterministic Rule: Regardless of review requests, if required check suites are failing, the PR is blocked on the author. Never ping reviewers for broken builds.
sim_5_trigger: @sarah-chen approved the pull request. All 4 CI checks are green, zero merge conflicts.
sim_5_nudge: PR is green and unblocked. Once the ready-to-merge window elapses, Baton reminds the author or a maintainer.
sim_5_rule: Deterministic Rule: Review approved + Checks success + Mergeable. No more review needed, someone just needs to press the green button.
